question: What is our status on everything DEQ?
raw:
**Most important:** Your air permit expires **November 15, 2026**. The Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit No. 26-2841-ST-01 set the renewal application deadline at July 18, 2026. You don't hold a copy of the renewal application or a DEQ receipt for it. Nothing in your files shows whether it was filed. Please confirm that first.

**What the permit file shows (Oregon DEQ)**

| Item | What the documents show |
|---|---|
| Permit | Expires 2026-11-15. The permit says not to operate after expiry without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application. |
| Renewal application (due 2026-07-18) | Not among your documents. |
| Semi-annual report, Jan–Jun 2026 (due 2026-07-31) | Not among your documents. |
| Annual report for 2025 | On file. DEQ's receipt is dated February 12, 2026. The receipt confirms receipt only. It is not a finding that the report is complete. |
| C-1 carbon replacement | The 2025 annual report set the next replacement for on or before March 14, 2026. No vendor record or invoice is on file. |
| Quarterly scrubber inspection (due 2026-09-30) | No record on file. The scrubber log doesn't show one. |
| Annual report for 2026 | Due 2027-02-15. |

**Gaps in the Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log (August–September 2026)**
- **Missing readings:** Daily readings for August 17–21 are missing for both scrubbers. Condition 3.1 asks for a reading every operating day.
- **Out-of-range reading:** On September 9, S-2 read 6.4 in. w.c. The limit is 6.0. The Notes column is blank, so there is no cause or corrective action.
- **Missing weekly check:** The weekly C-1 outlet check for the week of September 14 is missing. The week of September 28 check was due around October 2, and the log doesn't show it.
- **No sign-off:** No supervisor has signed the log.
- **No September totals:** September has no line-counter totals, so completeness can't be checked.

**What you didn't ask but need to know**
- **Deviation reporting:** The permit asks for DEQ notice within 24 hours of finding a deviation, then a written report within 15 days. The September 9 reading, and possibly the missing monitoring, may fall under this. Your files show no notice. Whether a notice is needed depends on what actually happened, so check with the people on the line.
- **Earlier deviation:** The 2025 annual report did report one deviation, the S-2 pump failure in August 2025.
- **Other permit conditions:** Nothing on file covers visible-emissions records, the annual fee payment, or the five-year record file.
- **Unread file:** The auditor checklist document (12-auditor-checklist-deq-air.docx) is still queued. I have no reading of it, so it isn't part of this answer.
- **Blank forms:** The DEQ inspection checklist and your Monthly EHS Self-Check are both blank templates. They are not records of anything done. The DEQ checklist is useful as a preview of what an inspector would ask to see.
- **Other state:** The state "Needs work" on the scrubber log, and the "Expiring" state on the permit, come from our readings dated 2026-10-14. If anything has been re-filed since, this answer may be out of date.

**What you could do next:** Look for the renewal application and DEQ's acknowledgment. If you find one, file it with the permit. If you can't find one, contact your DEQ Northwest Region permit writer today.
